review_notes: Inspected all 118 lines, the zero-ideal and coefficient-germ definitions, the finite-subscheme and Euler-difference proofs, relevant Mathlib instances, and downstream divisor uses. The finding concerns divisor construction, not generalizing the unweighted Euler-degree identity to arbitrary fields. No Lean execution was performed; proposed changes are source-supported but untested.

findings.excerpt:
theorem orderAt_finite_support
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)) [IsProper p] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (hDVR : ∀ x : X, x ≠ genericPoint X → IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (L : LineBundle X) (s : GlobalSections X L.sheaf) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    (Function.support (orderAt hDVR L s)).Finite := by
findings.problem: Finite support and the resulting divisor are restricted to proper complex curves, although the finiteness argument only needs a Noetherian underlying space and dimension at most one. This prevents using this divisor construction on regular affine curves or arithmetic curves without a proper complex structure map.
findings.proposed_change:
Under the existing `{X : Scheme.{0}} [IsIntegral X]`, generalize the statement to:
`theorem orderAt_finite_support [NoetherianSpace X] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (hDVR : ∀ x : X, x ≠ genericPoint X → IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (L : LineBundle X) (s : GlobalSections X L.sheaf) (hs : s ≠ 0) : (Function.support (orderAt hDVR L s)).Finite`.
Correspondingly expose:
`def divisor [NoetherianSpace X] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (hDVR : ∀ x : X, x ≠ genericPoint X → IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (L : LineBundle X) (s : GlobalSections X L.sheaf) (hs : s ≠ 0) : CurvePoint X →₀ ℕ`.
For the proof, put `I := SectionZeroIdeal.zeroIdeal L s`. As in `finite_subscheme_of_curve`, use `zeroIdeal_ne_bot` and `support_eq_top_iff` to show its support is not all of X; apply `proper_closed_finite_of_dimension_one hd I.support.isClosed`, then transfer finiteness through `I.range_subschemeι` and the injectivity of `I.subschemeι`. The remainder of the current proof is unchanged. Define the generalized divisor with `Finsupp.ofSupportFinite` and generalize its application lemma accordingly. Existing proper-complex wrappers and the Euler theorem can obtain the required Noetherian-space instance by the same compactness/local-Noetherian construction already used in `finite_subscheme_of_curve`. Retain `hs : s ≠ 0`; empty zero loci and dimension-zero integral schemes require no additional assumption.
findings.benefit: Makes effective section divisors available on nonproper Noetherian integral curves, independently of a base field or chosen structure map, while preserving the existing complex-curve application.
